description: Navajo Nation: Hotter, Drier Climate Puts Sand Dunes on the Move is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Navajo Nation; USGS Navajo Land Use Planning Project; Northern Arizona University | Institute for Tribal Environmental Professionals | Environmental Education Outreach Program. Sand dunes cover roughly one-third of the Navajo Reservation in northeastern Arizona. Higher temperatures and lower precipitation totals projected for the region have researchers monitoring dune motion and considering solutions. Coverage: Arizona (2015). The toolkit gives Arizona as the location, 2015 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open.
